answer: One concrete mechanism: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because hollow only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, fable is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any comet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
